notes: Use-case: enterprise customer support + downstream risk-scoring/reranking for trade surveillance — mixed workload (chat heavy during market hours, batch reranking overnight).

Performance asks (negotiation focus): minimum sustained throughput 30,000 tokens/sec across reserved pool; concurrency cap target 200 active streams; allowable short bursts up to 3x baseline for up to 5 minutes without pre-approval.
Latency SLOs: target p95 end-to-end response <400ms for single-turn chat; token-level p95 <20ms; legal insists on p99 visibility and incident escalation flow.

Reserved GPU planning: initial ask = reservation equivalent to 8x A100-80GB (two shards) to hit sustained throughput, with documented token/sec per-GPU profiles. Wants explicit headroom for batch reranks (overnight) and a fast path for scheduled capacity increases (15-min notice).

POC summary: 15 Feb perf demo via dedicated pool — Redwood delivered ~28k sustained tokens/sec at baseline with tight variance; small gaps during synthetic spike tests (burst policy triggered). Customer said: "close, but we need firm numbers before legal signs off".
Cost sensitivity: high — finance team modeling $/1000 tokens vs current on-prem spend. Interested in Optimize recommendations (quantization + batching) to reduce ARR.
Security: must pass full vendor risk questionnaire (completed v1), needs KMS integration + audit log export to SIEM, and data residency in us-east-1 for primary dataset.
Quote from CTO (on call 2026-02-15): "We need predictable tail behavior — if you promise a floor, we need penalties or credits when you miss it. Burst is fine only if bounded and observable."

Negotiation points open: SLA uptime target and financial remedy, precise definition of tokens/sec (measured at ingress vs served), how caching/prefix reuse counts toward guarantee, and whether preemptible/spot-backed capacity can count toward baseline.
